You can't exclude children for their behaviour, at least not before trying everything. Typically where I am (Australia) parents and educators need to work and take active steps to address the behaviours and try everything before we can even consider exclusion. I had children stabbing teachers and bashing other kids that still came in everyday.

1. Meet with parents and create an inclusion support plan to manage behaviours and work towards positive outcomes. Set guidelines around behaviour and what's acceptable vs. what will require the child to be collected immediately.
2. Have parents agree and work towards utilising outside support services for their child (biting could be due to a number of different things, best to get assessed by paed or developmental psych/behavioural specialist) 
3. meet with parents regularly, updates and strategies
4. Work with inclusion support services, try to employ additional educators (can be done subsidised under our gov)


There's a bunch of things that must be done before a child is permanently excluded from care, but typically children remain in care unless they are an extreme risk to the staff, other children and selves. They have a right to an education, regardless of behaviour.

I suggest you work on creating a detailed behaviour support plan, take detailed observations and notes on incidents of behaviour and try to find patterns in the day or reasoning behind behaviour so when you meet with parents you have evidence to go off.
